title: A Cleveland night: ribs, champagne and dancing a rumba
summary: After ribs and champagne with Duke he danced a rumba in a hotel cabaret, and his clothes were stolen.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: And then there's this picture of you with the band -- I think that's from a film, isn't it?
This is at the Cotton Club.
This is at the Cotton Club?
Yeah.
Okay, this is the picture on page ...
He used to come around and be just, you know, to play around.
That's on page 96 of the Gammon book, the picture is from at the Cotton Club. Ohio. (Interruption)
Uh-huh. Duke and his old lady, what's her name? Eve?
Evie, yeah.
He went to a place where they used
to sell ribs, very good, you know? We went there and got some ribs, and Duke was drinking champagne, and backed it up with some brandy, you know?
Yeah.

So naturally, I was with him, and we three were in there drinking, and eating these ribs, and I was a little off, you know? So I got into a taxicab to go to the hotel, and when I got there, I couldn't see the hotel; I told the taxi driver to keep on going, you know? So when I came back, I went to the cabaret that was downstairs in the hotel, it's a colored hotel, you know?

I went downstairs, and I don't know how I got so to tell him to play some Spanish music, but I did -- a rumba, or something, and I got one of the entertainers and I said, 'Would you like to dance with me?' But you do what I tell you. You know.

So she says, 'Sure, come on, let's go'. And Snake Hips was in there that day, in the cabaret, and I went over there and started doing my business, I don't know what I was doing, but whatever I did, I got a lot of big hand, you know? That's whiskey doing it, though, you know -- champagne doing it.
I didn't have the tape recorder on when you told me where it was. Where did you say this was? What city was this?
In Cleveland, Ohio.
Do you remember the name of the cabaret where you danced?

Oh, that was the Hotel ... gee, I forgot the name of the hotel. I don't know the name of the hotel, it was in the colored district. We were living there, and I was living there, too. That's where they stole my clothes while I was there.
Who stole your clothes?
Somebody!
In Cleveland.
In Cleveland, yeah.
Out of your hotel room?

Yeah. Somebody got in there and got all my shirts and everything like that. My bathrobe that she had just bought me for Christmas -- a bathrobe and something else. And when I was getting ready to go, to quit there and they was going to get out of town, they still gave me a bill for the room, and I said, "I'm not going to pay any bill for the room."
Of course not.

I said that you people were responsible. They stole more money than my rent could ever amount to. So I just told them to do whatever you wanted, but I'm walking away from here with my suitcase and I'm not paying. And I didn't pay, either.
